# NAVIG Spaces

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-spaces-readme.mjs from registry.json — edit the registry, then re-run. -->

A **space** is a whole workshop: a folder with a `.navig/` holding the agents, skills,
workflows, plans and example memory for one domain. Install one, then switch to it:

```bash
navig space install github:navig-run/registry/spaces/<folder>
navig space use <folder>
```

**44 spaces** — 41 listable (24 active, 15 planned, 2 labs, 0 ready) and 3 internal templates.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `active` | Ships working agents, skills and workflows |
| `ready` | Complete, not yet in wide use |
| `planned` | A designed scaffold — capabilities are still to be built; never sold |
| `labs` | Experimental and opt-in; never sold |

## Templates (internal)

- [`empty-space`](empty-space/) — The canonical blank skeleton `navig space init` starts from — a template, not a product
- [`example-space`](example-space/) — Fully annotated reference space showing the canonical structure every space gets from `navig space init`
- [`build-in-public-space`](build-in-public-space/) — Build-in-public workflow space — bootstrap stub, purpose not yet authored

## Create a space

```bash
cp -r empty-space/ my-space/            # the skeleton
# edit my-space/.navig/space.json — id must equal the folder name
navig space doctor my-space              # check it
node ../scripts/check-registry.mjs      # the publish gate
```

The manifest fields are documented in [`schema.yaml`](schema.yaml). Every space ships a
`LICENSE` (MIT), a `.navig/space.json`, and only *example* state under `.navig/memory/`,
`.navig/inbox/` and `.navig/state/`.

## Everyday commands

```bash
navig space list
navig space use <folder>
navig space current
navig space doctor
```
